In order to calculate \[\int {{CT:0}} d{{CT:1}}\] we can use the substitution \(u={{CT:2}}\).

So, if \(u = {{CT:2}}\) then \({{CT:3}} = {{CT:4}}\) and \(d{{CT:5}} = {{CT:6}} d{{CT:1}}\), so, \(d{{CT:1}} = d{{CT:5}}/{{CT:6}} = d{{CT:5}}2({{CT:4}})\).

Hence,

\[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle
 \int {{CT:0}} d{{CT:1}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  \int \frac{1}{u} d{{CT:5}}2({{CT:4}}) \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  \int {{CT:7}}d{{CT:5}} \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  \int {{CT:8}}d{{CT:5}} \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:9}} \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:10}}
 \end{array}\]
